analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: The equity index impact of SpaceX inclusion so far
key_insights: SpaceX free float has risen to roughly a third of shares, up from 5% at IPO, as lock-ups expired. GS estimates about half of shares will be in the float by mid-2027, consistent with precedent from large low-float IPOs.

Passive ETFs owned roughly $30B of SpaceX at end of October (about 1.5% of total market cap), with roughly $20B attributable to Nasdaq-100 benchmarked funds. GS expects upcoming rebalances to add modest further weight.

SpaceX is not in the S&P 500. Inclusion requires 12 months public and positive GAAP net income for the latest quarter and the trailing four quarters. On consensus forecasts the profit test is met after Q2 2027 results, pointing to possible inclusion in H2 2027 unless a corporate action such as a merger with a current constituent accelerates it.

The Nasdaq-100 weights constituents with float below 33% at 3x float market cap, and uses full listed market cap once float exceeds 33%. This makes the index weight less sensitive to further float increases than in other indices.
The next Russell 1000 Growth rebalance is December 11. GS estimates that a rebalance run today would create over $10B of additional demand from benchmarked passive ETFs.

SpaceX's effect on Nasdaq-100 fundamentals has been much smaller than investors expected. Excluding SpaceX, the index P/E would be less than half a turn lower (19.2x vs 19.5x), and return and volatility would be very similar. GS compares this to Tesla's 2020 S&P 500 inclusion.

Insiders and stakeholders held roughly 70% of SpaceX at end of June, hedge funds, mutual funds and ETFs about 5%, and non-filers (likely mostly individuals) about 25%. GS says insiders and individuals likely still own the majority of shares.

The S&P 500 traded flat in the few weeks around the five largest IPOs of the past 30 years before resuming its upward trend. GS notes the sample is small and the June 2026 market had competing factors.
GS S&P 500 forecasts: 8,000 at YE 2026, 8,700 at 12 months. EPS of $375 for 2026, $415 for 2027 and $460 for 2028, versus bottom-up consensus of $369, $426 and $497.
The S&P 500 fell 4.7% on the week. Semiconductors fell 19.7% and Information Technology fell 12.0%, while Consumer Staples gained 3.6% and Real Estate gained 2.5%.

Q3 2026 earnings season: 88% of S&P 500 companies have reported, 62% beat on equal-weighted EPS and 8% missed. Information Technology had 80% positive EPS surprises. On a cap-weighted basis 60% beat and 13% missed.

GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is 0.6, between the 'light' (below -1.0) and 'stretched' (above 1.0) thresholds. The S&P 500 forward P/E is 18x and the 10 largest companies are 39% of S&P 500 market cap.
The largest weekly moves among S&P 500 stocks: AppLovin +71%, and Seagate, Marvell, Western Digital (each -28%) and Sandisk (-27%) among the bottom ten.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 season as of 6 Nov: 439 of 500 companies reported (88%). Equal-weighted EPS: 62% positive, 8% negative, 30% in line, average surprise 7%. Revenue: 50% positive, 11% negative, average surprise 2%.
Cap-weighted S&P 500 Q3 2026: 81% of weight reported, 60% positive EPS surprises, 13% negative, average surprise 2%. Revenue was 56% positive and 5% negative.

Equal-weighted Q3 positive EPS surprise rates by sector: Information Technology 80%, Health Care 78%, Consumer Staples 77%, Industrials 69%, Real Estate 30%, Materials 29%. Comparison with earlier seasons: Q2 2026 69%, Q1 2026 65%, Q4 2025 55%, Q3 2025 66%.

The universe of comparable large IPOs is small, and June 2026 market performance had competing factors, so the historical IPO comparison is a weak guide.
Semiconductor and hardware names fell sharply this week (Semis -19.7%, Tech Hardware -7.7%), and the market is narrow with the top 10 stocks at 39% of S&P 500 market cap.

tension_points.bull_case: Concerns about SpaceX distorting index fundamentals were overstated. Excluding it, Nasdaq-100 P/E would be about 0.3x lower (19.2x vs 19.5x), and return, volatility and concentration are nearly unchanged.
tension_points.bear_case: Float is rising from 5% to about a third and toward half by mid-2027, so index weights and passive ownership will keep growing. A Russell 1000 Growth rebalance on Dec 11 could add over $10B of demand, and S&P 500 inclusion may follow in H2 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A corporate action such as a merger with an S&P 500 constituent could accelerate S&P 500 inclusion ahead of H2 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: SpaceX's index weights and passive ownership should keep rising with free float, but the effect on index fundamentals has been much smaller than investors expected.
theme_stances.evidence: much smaller impact on equity indices than many investors expected
